experiments.hypothesis: M1 (truncation-at-horizon bootstrap) reproduces ~45% Normal success in-framework and serves as the registry anchor for all later comparisons.
3-step TD returns propagate the delayed shortage/survival signal faster than 1-step, raising success above the M1 anchor.
With the value function now bootstrapped at the horizon, a longer effective horizon (gamma 0.995) lets the critic value stock buffers many days ahead and cuts residual shortage days.
Capping per-route outbound at 50% of stock shrinks the harmful part of the action space and prevents the single stock-stripping move that causes the remaining ~1 shortage day.

reasons: Keep the in-framework M1 anchor: despite prior manual evidence, a matched registry baseline is necessary for attribution.

The n-step and gamma variants are plausible, high-priority changes that preserve task realism, but they must use the same seeds and full late-convergence budget as the anchor; single-seed or short-run results are screens only and cannot establish improvement.

Drop m1_sendcap50: the arbitrary 50% cap changes the feasible control problem, may block necessary emergency transfers, and is unsupported by evidence that residual shortages come from stock-stripping actions. Diagnose action traces or sweep a realism-justified cap before spending a full run.

experiments.hypothesis: In-framework M1 (truncation-at-horizon bootstrap) reproduces the ~45% Normal-ops success and serves as the matched registry baseline for attributing all deltas below.
2-step returns on top of M1 propagate the delayed shortage/survival signal faster and beat the matched anchor on success_fraction.
3-step returns give more credit-assignment reach than n=2 without excessive off-policy bias, further lifting success_fraction over the anchor.

With the value function now stationary post-bootstrap, gamma=0.995 (effective horizon ~200d > the 100d episode) values end-of-episode stock-outs more strongly and reduces residual shortage days versus the anchor.

reasons: The four-way matched batch is scientifically useful, but the execution protocol is underspecified given known late convergence and high seed variance. Set a convergence-compatible budget reaching at least the prior ~500-generation checkpoint region; do not prune from an apparent early plateau.
Use a shared screening seed only for triage, then confirm any apparent winner and the M1 anchor on multiple matched seeds before claiming improvement.

Keep the gamma experiment exploratory, but revise its rationale: an effective discounted horizon exceeding 100 days does not by itself prove better end-of-episode stock-out valuation, especially when truncation bootstrapping imposes continuing-task semantics across a reset boundary.
Evaluate all variants with identical checkpoint selection and evaluation seeds/episodes to avoid attributing evaluation noise or selection bias to n-step or gamma changes.

experiments.hypothesis: n-step returns (TD_N_STEPS=3) propagate the delayed shortage/survival signal faster than 1-step TD, raising Normal-ops success over M1 at equal budget.
Selecting checkpoints on shortage_days instead of return aligns model selection with the primary goal (zero-shortage episodes) and lifts success_fraction without any learning change.
Capping per-route outbound at MAX_SEND_FRAC=0.5 prevents over-draining a hub in a single day, removing a common cause of the remaining ~1 shortage day.
Now that the value function is bootstrapped at the horizon, a longer effective horizon (GAMMA=0.995) lets the critic value multi-day stock buffers and reduces shortages.

reasons: TD_N_STEPS=3 directly tests a prioritized, untried mechanism for propagating delayed shortage signals.
MAX_SEND_FRAC=0.5 is a plausible operational constraint and tests whether limiting abrupt hub depletion improves Normal operations, though feasibility must be checked in evaluation.
GAMMA=0.995 is a clean, non-duplicate test of longer-horizon stock valuation after the truncation bootstrap fix.
m1_select_shortage_days is not approved because checkpoint selection is harness-owned and therefore not a valid proposal-controlled experiment.
